body.p: This amendment responds to the office action mailed June 14, 2024. In the office action the Examiner:
* objected to claims 11 and 21 for containing informalities;
* rejected claims 1, 3, 5, 8-10, 12, and 15-20 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable
over Nakamura et al. (US 2019/0298202 Al), in view of Varcoe et al. (US
* rejected claims 2, 11, 14, and 21 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over
Nakamura, in view of Varcoe as applied to claims 1 and 8, respectively, above, and
further in view of Ledbetter et al. (US 2020/0256929 Al);
* rejected claim 7 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Nakamura, in view
of Varcoe as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of Ishiyama et al. (US
* rejected claim 13 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Nakamura, in view
of Varcoe as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of Zuckerman et al. (US
* objected to claims 4 and 6 as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would
be allowable if rewritten in independent form.

Applicant's attorneys thank Primary Examiner Mattson for the opportunity to discuss the application during a telephone interview on July 25, 2024 with Douglas Crisman. In the interview, we discussed the rejection of claim 7 under 35 U.S.C. 103. The Examiner suggested that the Applicant include an argument as to why sensor spacings need to be different to detect both patient signals and background signals than just patient signals. No specific agreement was reached.
Independent claims 1 and 15 have each been amended to include the subject matter of claim 7. No new matter has been added.
Claims 6, 11, 16, and 21 have been amended to correct informalities. No new matter has been added.
Claim 7 has been canceled.
Claim 22 has been added. New claim 22 is an independent system claim that includes
the features of original system claim 15 and allowable claim 4. No new matter has been
added.
With respect to all amendments, Applicant has not dedicated or abandoned any
unclaimed subject matter. Moreover, Applicant has not acquiesced to any characterizations
of the invention, nor any rejections or objections of the claims, made by the Examiner.
Moreover, the Applicant hereby rescinds any prior disclaimer of claim scope, to the extent
they exist, made during the prosecution of this application or made during the prosecution of
any patent or other related patents/applications, and advises the Examiner that any such
previous disclaimers and the cited references that they were made to avoid may need to be
revisited.
After entry of this amendment, the pending claims are: claims 1-6 and 8-22.
Paragraph [0002] of the specification has been amended to include the application
number of a related patent application.
I. OBJECTED TO CLAIMS 11 AND 21 FOR CONTAINING INFORMALITIES
Amended claims 11 and 21 each recites "a diamond nitrogen vacancy (NV)
magnetometer."
Applicant respectfully requests that the claim objections be withdrawn.
II. REJECTION OF CLAIMS 1, 3,5, 8-10, 12, AND 15-20 UNDER 35 U.S.C. 103 AS BEING
UNPATENTABLE OVER NAKAMURA, IN VIEW OF VARCOE
In this Response, each of the independent claims 1 and 15 has been amended to
include the features of claim 7. The amended claims require "the plurality of magnetometers
are spatially distributed such that in Fourier space the ... magnetometers have a wavevector
coverage to recover information from both the biomagnetic field from the subject's organ and the background magnetic field."
The Office Action agrees that "Nakamura fails to teach that the magnetometers are distributed such that in Fourier space they have a wavevector coverage." Office Action at p.
9. This feature is also missing from Ishiyama, which is cited by the Office Action for allegedly disclosing the features of claim 7.

In Ishiyama, "[a]n organism magnetic signal [is] detected by the SQUID magnetic sensor" "within a magnetic shield room 11." See Ishiyama at 34, 35, and 38 and FIG. 1 (emphasis added). Because Ishiyama teaches detecting magnetic signals in a magnetically shielded room, Ishiyama does not teach measuring background magnetic fields. Furthermore, because the magnetic signals of the subject are measured in a magnetically shielded room in Ishiyama, the presence of magnetic shielding would reduce the strength of the background signal to the point that it is negligible and does not need to be cancelled to detect the subject's biological signals.

By contrast, the amended claims require that the apparatus be configured to "operate without magnetic shielding," such that during the operation of the apparatus, the magnetometers detect biomagnetic fields from a subject's organ in the presence of background magnetic field from the earth." See Applicant's Specification as filed at 13. "[T]he strength of the Earth's magnetic field is approximately 50 micro Teslas, which is about a million times larger in amplitude than the expected signal of the heart's magnetic field when [a magnetically unshielded] MCG device is positioned just outside the chest of a human subject." Id. at 11. Spatially distributing the magnetometers "such that in Fourier space, the ... magnetometers have a wavevector coverage to recover information from both the biomagnetic field from the subject's organ and the background magnetic field" as recited in the claims enhances both the detection of magnetic field signals from the target organ and allows for the application of signal processing techniques to reduce/remove signals from interference sources. Id. at 16 and amended claims.

Thus, for at least the above reasons, amended claims 1 and 15 and their associated dependent claims 3, 5, 8-10, 12, and 16-20 are patentable over the cited combination of Nakamura, Varcoe, and Ishiyama.
Applicant respectfully requests that these rejections be withdrawn.
III. REJECTION OF CLAIMS 2,11, 14, AND 21 UNDER 35 U.S.C.103 AS BEING UNPATENTABLE
OVER NAKAMURA, IN VIEW OF VARCOE AS APPLIED TO CLAIMS 1 AND 8, RESPECTIVELY,
ABOVE, AND FURTHER IN VIEW OF LEDBETTER
Claims 2, 11, 14, and 21 depend from respective independent claims 1 and 15, and

thus they include all the features of the independent claims by virtue of their dependency. As discussed above, Nakamura, Varcoe, and Ishiyama do not teach or suggest all the features of the amended independent claims. Furthermore, Ledbetter is not cited for, and does not teach,
the features of the amended independent claims that are missing from Nakamura, Varcoe, and
Ishiyama. Thus, claims 2, 11, 14, and 21 are patentable over the cited combination of
Nakamura, Varcoe, Ishiyama, and Ledbetter.
Applicant respectfully requests that these rejections be withdrawn.
IV. REJECTION OF CLAIM 7 UNDER 35 U.S.C. 103 AS BEING UNPATENTABLE OVER
NAKAMURA, IN VIEW OF VARCOE AS APPLIED TO CLAIM 1 ABOVE, AND FURTHER IN
Claim 7 has been canceled, thus rendering its rejection moot.
V. REJECTION OF CLAIM 13 UNDER 35 U.S.C. 103 AS BEING UNPATENTABLE OVER
NAKAMURA, IN VIEW OF VARCOE AS APPLIED TO CLAIM 1 ABOVE, AND FURTHER IN
Claim 13 depends from claim 1 and thus it includes all the features of the independent
claim by virtue of its dependency. As discussed above, Nakamura, Varcoe, and Ishiyama do
not teach or suggest all the features of amended claim 1. Furthermore, Zuckerman is not cited
for, and does not teach, the features of amended claim 1 that are missing from Nakamura,
Varcoe, and Ishiyama. Thus, claim 13 is patentable over the cited combination of Nakamura,
Varcoe, Ishiyama, and Zuckerman.
Applicant respectfully requests that these rejections be withdrawn.
VI. OBJECTION TO CLAIMS 4 AND 6 AS BEING DEPENDENT UPON A REJECTED BASE CLAIM,

body.p: The Applicant thanks the Examiner for indicating the allowability of claims 4 and 6.
In this Response, Applicant has added a new independent claim 22 that includes the
features of original independent claim 15 and allowable claim 4. Applicant respectfully
requests that the Examiner consider new claim 22 with a view toward allowance. Applicant
has amended independent claims 1 and 15 in another way.
VII. NEW CLAIM 22
New claim 22 is an independent system claim that includes the features of original
system claim 15 and allowable claim 4. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests that the
Examiner consider new claim 22 with a view toward allowance.

By responding in the foregoing remarks only to particular positions asserted by the Examiner, the Applicants do not necessarily acquiesce in other positions that have not been explicitly addressed. In addition, the Applicants' arguments for the patentability of a claim should not be understood as implying that no other reasons for the patentability of that claim exist.

In light of the above amendments and remarks, the Applicants respectfully request that the Examiner reconsider this application with a view towards allowance. The Examiner is invited to call the undersigned attorney at (650) 843-4000, if a telephone call could help resolve any remaining items.
Respectfully submitted,
